answer_text:
Let

\[
r_1=2+2\sin\theta
\]

be the cardioid and

\[
r_2=4\sin\theta
\]

be the other curve.

First identify the second curve:

\[
r=4\sin\theta \implies r^2=4r\sin\theta \implies x^2+y^2=4y
\]

\[
x^2+(y-2)^2=4
\]

So \(r=4\sin\theta\) is a circle of radius \(2\) centered at \((0,2)\), with area

\[
A_{\text{circle}}=\pi(2)^2=4\pi.
\]

Now compare the two polar radii for \(0\le \theta\le \pi\):

\[
r_1-r_2=(2+2\sin\theta)-4\sin\theta=2(1-\sin\theta)\ge 0.
\]

Thus the circle lies inside the cardioid in the upper half-plane. For \(\pi\le\theta\le 2\pi\), the circle has no positive-\(r\) points, so the lower part of the cardioid is also outside the circle. Therefore the desired area is the area of the cardioid minus the area of the circle.

The area of the cardioid is

\[
A_{\text{cardioid}}
=\frac12\int_0^{2\pi} (2+2\sin\theta)^2\,d\theta.
\]

Expand:

\[
(2+2\sin\theta)^2=4+8\sin\theta+4\sin^2\theta.
\]

So

\[
A_{\text{cardioid}}
=\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}\left(4+8\sin\theta+4\sin^2\theta\right)\,d\theta.
\]

Using

\[
\int_0^{2\pi}\sin\theta\,d\theta=0,
\qquad
\int_0^{2\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta=\pi,
\]

we get

\[
A_{\text{cardioid}}
=\frac12\left(8\pi+0+4\pi\right)
=6\pi.
\]

Therefore the required area is

\[
A=6\pi-4\pi=2\pi.
\]

\[
\boxed{2\pi}
\]
